description:
pkix-ct/tests/fixtures/sct-oracle/gen_*.py scripts and tests/fixtures/live-log/capture_live_log.py implement multi-source oracle generation:
- gen_x509_entry_sct.py: pyca/cryptography signs, hand-rolls RFC 6962 §3.2 wire format, openssl verifies independently.
- gen_precert_entry_sct.py: same pyca-based oracle PLUS an in-script DER walker that strips the SCT-list extension and asserts it matches the cryptography-emitted no-ext TBS bytes (self-test of the oracle itself).
- gen_merkle_inclusion.py: RFC 6962 §2.1 reference algorithm AND RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2 verify algorithm (different code path) both compute root_hash; oracle internal-consistent.
- gen_sth_oracle.py: pyca signs, openssl independently verifies.
- capture_live_log.py: real CT log get-proof-by-hash response, three independent paths (Python computes leaf_hash from RFC text, CT log accepts that leaf_hash for query, Python verifier reconstructs root, openssl verifies STH signature).

Every single test fixture has at least one independent oracle path; precert and merkle have two; live_log has three. This matches workspace AGENTS.md test-integrity rule: 'tests must have an independent oracle: known test vectors from an external source, cross-validation between two independent implementations, or bit-exact comparison against a reference path.'

A future contributor might suggest 'simplify by removing the openssl cross-check, the pyca-only oracle is sufficient' or 'drop the live_log capture since gen_precert_entry_sct already covers the precert flow.' Both would weaken the test discipline. The redundant oracles are the entire point — they catch implementation bugs that a single-oracle harness would miss.

Defend this aggressively. The cost of the redundant oracles is one-time Python script effort; the cost of removing them is the risk of a CVE.
title: Three-layer independent oracle for fixtures (pyca + openssl + hand-rolled DER walker) is exactly the test discipline workspace policy demands
